title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
summary:
The government just issued two new aviation safety rules for certain Airbus jets, and also clarified timing for a separate small‑business lending requirement. The aviation updates aim to reduce rare but high‑risk scenarios in flight; the lending note outlines how some banks determine when they must start reporting data.

For airlines operating Airbus A330 and A340 models, the Federal Aviation Administration is ordering immediate updates to flight manuals and dispatch rules when flying with the landing gear down or when a landing gear fault message appears. The concern is that very cold air could damage brake system parts during gear‑down flight, and that taking off with a known gear retraction fault could, in the worst case after a total engine shutdown, cut off emergency electrical power. These changes take effect October 17, 2025, and comments are invited through November 17. The agency estimates about 153 U.S. airplanes are affected and pegs the paperwork cost at roughly $170 per aircraft.

A second rule covers certain Airbus Canada A220 aircraft. An investigation found that a change in a small sealing part increased electrical resistance where wires pass through a bulkhead, which could make the airplane more vulnerable to electromagnetic interference or lightning. Operators must test the electrical connection at a specific location and, if needed, add bonding plates to restore proper protection. That rule takes effect November 6, 2025.

Who benefits? Passengers and flight crews gain from reduced safety risks, and airlines get clearer procedures for edge cases that are uncommon but critical. The A220 fix should also lower the chance of electrical upset from outside sources. On the lending side, small businesses and policymakers benefit from more consistent data on access to credit, and lenders get concrete examples on how to judge their reporting tier and deadlines.

Who might be negatively affected? Airlines with affected fleets will face new checks, manual updates, and tighter dispatch conditions that could add minor costs or occasional delays. Maintenance teams will have added testing and possible hardware installs on the A220. Lenders subject to the small‑business data rule may see added compliance work and costs, which some could pass through to customers in the short term.
